reason: Use Tier 2: add a hard-negative ranking term to the successful tied-embedding masked transformer. The 0.5800 reference outperformed relative bias (0.5725), R-Drop (0.5650), and untied embeddings (0.5363), favoring preservation of its representation. Sampled softmax does not explicitly emphasize the strongest competing candidates; testing that objective limitation offers a distinct, controlled direction, although the trajectory does not establish the plateau’s cause.

plan.model_design: Restore the original 0.5800 tied-embedding MaskedSASRec configuration as the experimental base, training from scratch without relative bias, R-Drop, or output_emb. Make one experimental change to its loss: for each supervised position, add 0.1 times the mean softplus(negative_logit - positive_logit) over the 10 highest-scoring valid negatives from the existing 256 sampled negatives. Exclude accidental target matches before selecting hard negatives, compute the ranking term in float32, and preserve equal weighting between final-mask and auxiliary-position objectives. This concentrates additional gradient on competitors near the recommendation boundary while retaining sampled-softmax supervision, the jointly trained item_bias, and one jointly trained network per category. Preserve MaskedSASRec.__init__, forward(sequence), predict(sequence, candidates), prediction_sequence, existing variable names, and all architecture and sampling settings.
plan.training_evaluation: Implement the combined objective within the existing single forward/backward training step, preserving optimizer settings, training seed 42, worker seeding, supplied splits, and the SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Preserve fixed validation using 200 users per category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42; select one checkpoint by the existing HR@10/NDCG ordering and compare authoritative host macro HR@10 against 0.5800 without assuming improvement. Update architecture_spec, validate_metadata, and write_predict_script to describe the tied architecture and hard-negative objective, strictly load one checkpoint per category, and verify exported scores against that checkpoint with identical history processing. Remove obsolete conflict fragments rather than retaining them inside strings, and check finite loss and gradients when sampled negatives contain duplicates or target collisions. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, existing patience and time limits, and the final validation-score print; leave held-out inference to the host without reading test files or generating a synthetic submission.
